findings.evidence: Enumerated by scanning core.json feats for archetype==='spell-trickster' (26 hits). Dedication print (feat-3368) sets the whole lane's shape: "Whenever you gain a feat from this archetype, you either learn to modify the effects of a single spell… Each time you Cast the Spell corresponding to the feat you chose, you decide whether to cast its normal or modified version… Besides modifications mentioned in the feat, the spell functions as normal." That is exactly a spellNotes clause: it never changes a sheet number, it is a per-cast alternative the player reads on the spell.

Print (feat-3369): "When you cast _mage hand_, you can modify its target to be a set of [thieves' tools]… the tools move up to 20 feet towards a device or lock. After you Sustain the Spell on future turns, you can use the tools to attempt Thievery checks to Disable a Device or Pick a Lock within the spell's range, but you take a –2 penalty… If you critically fail, the spell ends and you can't use this modification again for 24 hours." Remaster identity: core.spells has NO mage-hand; telekinetic-hand (rank 0, remaster, Player Core) is it, and our own prose already says so. Guard test passes without a NAMED_BY_OTHER_MEANS entry: core-descriptions feats.agile-hand.d opens "When you cast Telekinetic Hand", so `namesIt` matches. items.thieves-toolkit ships.

SCOPE: the 22 modify-a-spell feats sort as Agile Hand, Barrier Shield, Beacon Mark, Choking Smoke, Confounding Image, Directed Poison, Disk Rider, Forceful Push, Larcenous Hand, Lingering Flames, Obscured Terrain, Scattered Fire, Shining Arms, Siphoning Touch, Smoldering Explosion, Steal Vitality, Summon Ensemble, Surrounding Flames, Toppling Tentacles, Tracing Sigil, Uneasy Rest, Wild Lights (Animate Net / Drenching Mist / Volatile Grease excluded per brief; Spell Trickster Dedication is not a modify feat). I covered items 8-16, Forceful Push through Steal Vitality, so the middle third is fully covered under either a 7/8/7 or an 8/8/6 split — Forceful Push is a deliberate overlap with part 1's tail.

BIGGEST REFUTATION: the obvious NAMED_BY_OTHER_MEANS claim is WRONG for all nine feats. The prose shipped in public/core-descriptions.json is already fully remaster-renamed (mage hand -> "Telekinetic Hand", obscuring mist -> "Mist", vampiric touch -> "Vampiric Feast", and even "4th level" -> "4th rank"), so the guard at test/spell-notes.test.tsx:158-164 passes on prose.includes(spell.name) with no allowlist entry. The existing 'feats/disk-rider': ['carryall'] entry is the exception, not the pattern — disk-rider's .d still reads "When you cast Floating Disk". I verified this programmatically for all nine (spellShips=true, namesIt=true for each).

OTHER VERIFIED NEGATIVES: none of the nine has a spellNotes value in core.json or any existing row in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json; none has a `node`, so public/ast/*.json is NOT the render carrier for them and .d is what DescBody prints; none appears in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts, public/toggle-modes.json, or public/consumable-modes.json. The only src reference to any of them is src/rules/featPickGrants.ts:164, where forceful-push and shining-arms sit among the seven level-4 feats the dedication's double pick offers.

HOUSE STYLE the rows follow, taken from the five already-authored spell-trickster rows (confounding-image, disk-rider, volatile-grease, drenching-mist, animate-net): the note opens "<Feat Name>: " then continues lowercase, and calls the host spell "this spell" rather than repeating its name; heightened entries keep their inline **Heightened (X)** markers; a DIFFERENT spell referenced inside the clause keeps its name.

APPLY: append via a script that imports { readBackfill, writeBackfill } from scripts/lib/write-backfill.mjs — the stored 1-space-indent / CRLF / no-trailing-newline format is load-bearing for reviewable diffs — then regenerate public/core.json with the data build.

SCOPE / BOUNDARY. The archetype has 22 modify-a-spell feats (23 records minus the dedication). findings.spec:
ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by execution, not inference). scripts/lib/aon-facets.mjs:308-312 `bodyOf(rec)` strips only the FIRST `<title>` element and returns the ENTIRE rest of the AoN page — on a multi-variant page that is every sibling variant's text. `activationOf()` (aon-facets.mjs:415-418) and `frequencyOf()` (aon-facets.mjs:448-469) then take the FIRST regex match anywhere in that page-wide body. Both are emitted unconditionally in the items block at aon-facets.mjs:913-917 (`const act = activationOf(rec); if (act) facets.activationCost = act;` / `const freq = frequencyOf(rec); if (freq) facets.frequency = freq;`), consumed by scripts/import-core-v2.mjs:284 `overlayContent()` which spreads facets over every overlaid record.

REPRODUCTION (I ran it): loading C:/trying ai 2/hh-data-export/without-images/data/equipment.json and calling the exported frequencyOf/activationOf returns, for ALL 25 docs equipment-407 / -407-* : freq={max:1,per:'day'} act={type:'actions',value:1} — i.e. Pale Lavender Ellipsoid's line stamped onto every stone; and for ALL 15 docs equipment-3055 / -3055-* : freq={max:1,per:'hour'} — Sprouting's line stamped onto every stone. Also equipment-470-591 (Wayfinder of Rescue) act={type:'actions',value:1} leaked from a sibling wayfinder.

SCOPE (measured over equipment/weapon/armor/shield/relic exports): 10,001 item docs, 4,686 sit on a page with `<title level="2">` variant sections and resolve to their own section. Of those, 265 receive a `frequency` and 102 an `activationCost` whose first page match lies in a NON-BASE sibling section — an unambiguous cross-variant leak. (A looser count — value present but the record's own section has no line — is 1,331 / 698; the difference is the legitimate 'Greater X functions as X' inheritance from section 0.)

GUARD (apply-ready): the correct section-splitter ALREADY EXISTS in the same file — `heldSpellsOf` at aon-facets.mjs:499-538 builds `sections` from the `<title level="2">` marks and selects `norm(section.title) === norm(rec.name)`. Extract that into a shared `variantBodyOf(rec)` and route `activationOf`/`frequencyOf` through it:
  1. If the page has no level-2 marks -> current `bodyOf` behaviour (unchanged).
  2. If it has marks and `norm(rec.name)` matches a section -> scan ONLY that section; if that section has no `**Activate**` / `**Frequency**`, fall back to SECTION 0 (the base entry) only, then return null. Never a sibling.

SWEEP METHOD + COUNTS. Two independent passes, cross-checked. (1) Full AoN mirror (C:\wonderers guide\aon-2e-archive\data\by-category, all 100+ categories): 210 records match "Frequency <n> per|each|every <N> <unit>", of which 77 equipment + 6 item-bonus + 4 relic + 1 vehicle. FINAL TALLY: 48 affected item records (one finding each). Batch 18 named 15 name-groups = 21 records; 27 of the 48 are NEW. Distinct cadences: 47 records at "once (per|every) 10 minutes", 1 at "once every 30 minutes" (phylactery-of-faithfulness-greater — 30x too fast, the worst single case in the family). 4 already-done via label text (ring-of-sigils-greater, maestros-chair, primeval-mistletoe, primeval-mistletoe-greater) + a 5th of the same shape not previously named (restorative-handwraps).

THREE SUB-SHAPES WORTH KNOWING, all confirmed against print:
- Direct print: the Frequency line itself says "once per 10 minutes" (most records).
- GRADE RETUNE: the base item prints "**Frequency** once per day" and a grade paragraph rewrites it — "you can activate it once every 30 minutes" (phylactery), "the harness can be activated once every 10 minutes" (arachnid), "…once every 10 minutes" (unmemorable mantle, bracers), "a frequency of once per 10 minutes" (brooch), "once per 10 minutes" (ash gown). Foundry's variant description already applies the retune, so these DO reach the parser — 6 records that an aonId-keyed audit of the base page would wrongly clear.
- MULTI-ACTIVATION: the affected counter is not always `freq`. freq2 for lifes-last-breath / storm-flash / storm-flash-greater / dragonauts-wingsuit; freq3 for vambrace-of-gorum; all three for chimera-flail. buildCounters (import-core.mjs:695) numbers them in description order, so the mapping above is positional and must be preserved when writing the absolute-assignment overlay row.

DISPLAY-VISIBILITY (checked, per the AST rule): this is NOT a description-text defect — the printed cadence renders correctly. public/ast/items.json carries the node for these records and anchor-spear / chimera-flail contain the literal "10 minutes"; phylactery-of-faithfulness-greater contains "30 minutes" instead. So the player currently sees a description saying "once per 10 minutes" sitting directly above a pip labelled "per minute". No REPAIRS-table entry is warranted anywhere in this family.

CARRIER/READER CHAIN (verified end to end, no `as never` casts, no dead fields): ItemCounter (types.ts:3514-3525) -> counterDefs (itemUses.ts:25-48, spreads `...c`) -> itemCounters (itemUses.ts:51-60, EXPLICIT field whitelist at :58 — this is where a new field gets silently dropped) -> CounterUse (itemUses.ts:13-22) -> ItemDetail.tsx:426 `{u.label}` and InventoryTab.tsx:334 title / :336 + :347 aria-labels. `CounterUse.per` has NO numeric reader for items (play.ts:1962-1971 resets on `resetsOnRest` alone; there is no item analogue of featUses.ts:113 isSubDaily), so `label` is the whole player-visible story and `every` is added for machine truth and future consumers.

results.task: Audit scripts/held-spell-rank-check.mjs for its blind spot, measure every item the blind spot hides, spec per-item corrected spell ranks and the check-script widening.

findings.spec:
WHAT IT READS (verified line by line): (1) exactly ONE storage carrier — `item.heldSpells` (held-spell-rank-check.mjs:35-36 `const held = item?.heldSpells; if (!held || typeof held !== 'object') continue;`), the rank->ids map; (2) exactly ONE text carrier — `descs.items[id].d` (:37), matched by ONE forward-only regex `RANKED` (:29) that requires the number to sit IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the spell name and the name to be followed by `[.,;)]` or ` as|and|from|with|at|on`.

WHAT IT MISSES:
(a) TEXT SHAPE — the reversed print form `You cast <Spell> at <N>th rank` / `as a <N>th-rank spell` / `heightened to <N>th level`. This is how the whole Treasure-Vault/Player-Core-2 OVERCHARGE WAND family is written, and it is where the 31 items below hide. Also blocked: a trailing noun (`4th-rank Dream Message spell.` -> slug `dream-message-spell`, silently dropped at :56), a space instead of a hyphen (`4th rank Wall of Wind`), `(` after the name (`3rd-rank Fear spell (DC 38)`), `Nth-level` instead of `Nth-rank`, and `A or B` lists (`2nd-rank Harm or Heal`).
(b) NAME/ID SHAPE — for the graded wand family the printed rank is carried by the VARIANT TITLE (`Wand of Teeming Ghosts (3rd-Rank Spell)`) while the body says only `of the indicated rank`. The check never reads `item.name`, so for these records there is no number in the prose to find at all.
(c) STORAGE SHAPES never opened: `item.spellSlot.rank` (144 items, live reader build.ts:6416-6417 `{ [item.spellSlot.rank]: [it.heldSpell] }` + ItemDetail.tsx:201 picker filter), `item.innateSpells[].rank` (65 items, live reader build.ts:6516 -> castRank build.ts:6586-6627 -> innateRep build.ts:6649), `item.resonant.innateSpells[].rank` (18 items, build.ts:6530), `item.spellNotes` (10 items), and the same `innateSpells` shape on feats (303) / heritages (13) / backgrounds (8).

WIDENING SPEC for scripts/held-spell-rank-check.mjs:
1. NAME LANE (new, catches all 31): if `/\((\d+)(?:st|nd|rd|th)[- ]Rank(?: Spell)?\)$/i` matches `item.name` (or the id tail `-(\d+)(st|nd|rd|th)-rank(-spell)?$`), that N is the printed rank for every NON-CANTRIP spell in `item.heldSpells`; report when no key equals N.
2. REVERSED PROSE LANE: per held spell, build a regex from `content.spells[sid].name` and match `<Name>( spell| cantrip)?[^.;]{0,60}?(?:at|as an?)\s+(\d+)(?:st|nd|rd|th)[- ](?:rank|level)` and `<Name>[^.;]{0,60}?heightened to (?:the )?(\d+)(?:st|nd|rd|th)[- ]?(?:rank|level)`.
3. FORWARD LANE FIX: allow `[- ]` between number and `rank`, accept `level` as a synonym, allow an optional trailing `spell|cantrip|ritual`, and widen the terminator set to `[.,;)(—–]` plus end-of-string.
4. CARRIER SWEEP: also walk `item.spellSlot.rank` (compare against the name lane — currently all 144 agree, so this lane starts green), `item.innateSpells[]` and `item.resonant.innateSpells[]` with effective rank = `g.rank ?? spells[sid].rank`, skipping grants that carry `heightenHalfLevel`/`heightenAt`/`heightenBySkill` (level-dependent, no single printed answer) and at-will cantrips (rank 0 by design, same reason the existing :59 cantrip guard exists).
5. DIRECTION RULE (memory rule, must be encoded, not just documented): for evidence drawn from DESCRIPTION PROSE, only `printed > stored` is evidence. Graded variants share ONE description body in this corpus, so a lower number in the text is the base variant's clause, not this record's. Concrete refutation: `greater-trident-of-the-azarketis` stores hydraulic-torrent at 6 and its `.d` contains "You cast a 5th-rank hydraulic torrent" (the Item-11 base clause) — the widened matcher flags it and it is CORRECT as stored, because the same `.d` also carries the greater's own clause. Evidence drawn from the record's OWN NAME is per-record and is safe in BOTH directions — that is the only lane allowed to report `stored > printed`, and it is what catches wand-of-pernicious-poison-1st-rank-spell.
6. Keep the existing `storedAt` Set-per-spell semantics (an item may legitimately hold one spell at several ranks) and the cantrip early-return.

results.notes:
SCOPE CORRECTION, stated plainly: the caller framed the blind spot as "a storage shape". It is more precisely a PRINT-EVIDENCE shape. The 31 items measured above are all stored in `items.heldSpells` — the carrier the check DOES read — and they escape because (a) their printed rank lives in the VARIANT TITLE (`Wand of Teeming Ghosts (3rd-Rank Spell)`) while the body says only "of the indicated rank", and (b) where HH's importer did substitute a number into the prose it wrote the REVERSED form ("You cast False Vitality at 3rd-rank"), which the `RANKED` regex at held-spell-rank-check.mjs:29 cannot match. The check never reads `item.name`. This is the "staff/wand charge structures" item on the caller's candidate list, and it is exactly 31 records (30 stored-below-print + 1 stored-above-print), matching the "~29" estimate.

THE GENUINE STORAGE BLIND SPOTS EXIST TOO, BUT ARE MOSTLY CLEAN — measured, not assumed:
- `item.spellSlot.rank` (144 items, live reader build.ts:6416-6417, ItemDetail.tsx:201/596/602). All 144 agree with their own name rank (scrolls 1st-10th, magic wands, Cyrusian/Continuation/Widening/Purification/Legerdemain/Mercy/Reaching/Hybrid Form/Spiritual Warfare/Thundering Echoes families). findings.spec: The `&& !/[ -]/.test(seg)` half of import-core.mjs:162 is unreachable. `/^[A-Za-z0-9]{12,}$/` is fully anchored and its character class excludes both space and hyphen, so any seg reaching the second test already contains neither. Dropping it changes no behaviour and removes the misleading suggestion that the rule tolerates multi-word names. The narrowed predicate in F1 already omits it.
findings.evidence: `/^[A-Za-z0-9]{12,}$/` anchored at both ends over a class with no space and no hyphen; `!/[ -]/.test(seg)` can therefore never be false when the first test is true.

METHOD. - 270 of the 273 sit in description prose (the other 3 — including the sole `Inextinguishable` — are in rule elements/flags and never reach a shipped description).
